summary: Phase 149O.18D -- AG5 Mandatory Consumption Integration: bounded production implementation phase (Wave D of the 149O.17 plan), mirroring 149O.18C's AG3 wiring exactly. Confirmed baseline: repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.18C completed/complete, HMRC-001 v1.0 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- CONFORMS, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Read HMRC-001, the 149O.18A/18B/18C phase documents, and build_rollback_execution in full (agent.py, pre-phase 94021-94249), independently re-inventoried every production caller (exactly one, commands/agent.py's pcae rollback --per-id dispatch). Wired 149O.18A's fresh resolve_production_hatp_cutover_mode and 149O.18B's real-effect evaluate_for_real_effect into build_rollback_execution's Mandatory Consumption Boundary, placed after every existing structural precondition (PER eligibility, payload availability, ECP lookup, in-progress conflict, divergence check, RER record persistence, dry_run early return) and immediately before the first real filesystem mutation (the restore/remove loop's write_text/write_bytes/unlink calls). AG5 has no legacy human-approval gate at all (unlike AG3), so no legacy-skip branch or earlier non-authoritative mode read was needed or added -- a deterministic HMRC ALLOW plus structural validity alone is sufficient to reach effect in HATP_MANDATORY. In HATP_MANDATORY, the boundary requires an explicit hatp_evidence_id, constructs an Ag5RollbackApprovalContext (already defined by 149O.17/18B specifically anticipating this phase, unmodified), calls evaluate_for_real_effect (never evaluate_for_advisory, statically and behaviorally confirmed), and requires pb_decision == DECISION_ALLOW before any mutation may run; missing/invalid evidence, PB DENY/HUMAN_REVIEW, raw hatp_proof/hatp_evidence parameters, a direct-function-call bypass, and a stale/reused prior-attempt decision all fail closed with zero mutation. dry_run returns before the RER record is even created and before the gate's insertion point -- zero mutation and zero HATP evaluation in every mode, since HMRC-001 assigns this module's advisory entrypoint no required role in AG5's dry-run reporting. Mode is read fresh, once, immediately before the evidence check (no cache, no earlier read to gate since there is no legacy branch to gate). While building this phase's own test suite -- the first ever to supply hatp_evidence_id to build_rollback_execution -- discovered and fixed two pre-existing, never-previously-exercised read_git_branch(str(root.path)) type-mismatch bugs (AttributeError), same category and same root cause 149O.18C fixed for AG3's own Wave-7 block: one in the pre-existing Wave-7 (149O.6) advisory hatp_authority block, one that this phase's own new gate would have introduced had it copied the same buggy call shape; both corrected to read_git_branch(root). Also added one new terminal RER status, aborted_hatp_mandatory_denied, to the existing closed _RER_VALID_STATUSES vocabulary, so a mandatory-gate denial persists the record in a genuine terminal state (with completed_at set) rather than leaving it stuck in_progress, which build_execution_chain_doctor's interrupted_rer check would otherwise flag; pre-existing status values are untouched. Authored 48 new tests across two files (22 in tests/test_ag5_hatp_mandatory_consumption.py: LEGACY_COMPATIBLE/PREPARED regression, dry-run non-mutation across every mode, missing/invalid-evidence fail-closed, PB DENY/HUMAN_REVIEW blocking, the real current POL-005 consequence confirmed end-to-end, deterministic-ALLOW effect, direct-call bypass prevention, raw-hook rejection, no-cache repeat-attempt re-evaluation via a second distinct PER, signature closure, effect-truthfulness (behavioral and static), gate-placement (AST source-position), and RER terminal-status persistence; 26 in tests/test_phase_149o_18d_ag5_mandatory_consumption_integration.py: production file allowlist -- exactly agent.py -- forbidden-file non-touch, 18A/18B/AG3/contract byte-identity, CLI/PB non-touch, effect-ordering and direct-call-coverage AST checks, no-advisory-call static check, no-real-activation check, RER status vocabulary, and read_git_branch call-signature fix confirmation), all added to Fast Green. Ran a full regression sweep (tests/test_agent.py -k rollback: 78/78 passed, byte-identical AG3/AG5 legacy behavior; the full -k "149o or hatp or rae or permission_broker" sweep A/B-diffed via git stash against the clean 149O.18C baseline: 37 pre-existing failures unrelated to this phase, confirmed identical with and without this phase's changes; exactly 10 newly-invalidated, 9 the identical mechanical zero-src/pcae/-diff-since-my-own-baseline snapshot pattern every historical HATP-lineage phase test already carries whenever a later phase touches agent.py, plus one, test_phase_149o_18c...::test_build_rollback_execution_source_unchanged_since_entry, that is legitimately and necessarily invalidated by this phase's own stated purpose -- no AG3/AG5/Permission-Broker behavioral regression found anywhere in the sweep). VERDICT: AG5 MANDATORY HATP CONSUMPTION INTEGRATION: IMPLEMENTED -- READY FOR 149O.18E. No CLI plumbing, no legacy approve-command change, and no Permission Broker/POL-005 change was made. HMRC-001 v1.0 and all six other upstream contracts remain byte-unchanged; 18A and 18B remain byte-unchanged; AG3's execute_rollback remains byte-unchanged. No real Cutover Record or HATP_MANDATORY activation occurred. B-149O-1..4 remain INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AT HATP-GATED AUTHORITY BOUNDARY -- SYSTEM EXECUTION CLOSURE DEFERRED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Recommended next phase: 149O.18E -- CLI + Legacy Authority Migration Integration.
